messages:
Asha (People Ops): Hi @all — quick policy update: we published revised Emergency Leave & Travel Reimbursement guidelines. TL;DR: employees get up to 5 days paid emergency PTO for immediate-family medical emergencies, plus expanded emergency travel reimbursements when approved (up to $1500 domestic / $3000 international). Full policy here: https://redwood.inc/policies/emergency-leave-v2. Please read before filing claims. :sparkles:

Jin: thanks! does this apply retroactively to trips booked last week? :eyes:

Asha (People Ops): Good question — yes, retroactive claims accepted for qualifying emergency travel that occurred within the last 30 days. Submit via the expense portal with receipts + short justification. For travel older than 30 days, we’ll evaluate case-by-case — escalate to People Ops. :+1:

Allison: Are contractors eligible for emergency travel reimbursement? We have a contractor on an urgent site visit for a family issue.

Asha (People Ops): Short answer: contractors are not automatically covered. If the contractor is on a Redwood-managed SOW and the PM requests it, we can consider one-off reimbursements. Please have the eng manager ping People Ops with the SOW details and reason.

Mike (Legal): Quick legal note: reimbursements > $2,000 require additional vendor paperwork for tax/compliance. If finance flags it, Legal will help collect the forms.

Grant (Finance): Filing details to speed approvals: use expense code `EMG-TRVL` and cost center 2105. Attach all receipts (PDF/photos). Put "emergency" and the family relationship in the notes field. Example entry you can paste into the expense form:

```
Expense Type: Airfare
Expense Code: EMG-TRVL
Cost Center: 2105
Amount: 1240.00
Notes: family emergency - last-minute flight change (parent hospitalization)
Receipt: attached.jpg
```

Asha (People Ops): Also new: for emergency seat upgrades (medical necessity) or caregiver accompaniment, reasonable reimbursement will be considered with receipts and a short justification. Prior approval preferred, but we’ll accept post-facto claims if it truly was an emergency.

Jin: what about visa/evac fees for internationals? those can be pricey.

Asha (People Ops): Visa/evacuation costs are eligible up to the international cap; for larger amounts, submit as an exception request and tag Finance + People Ops. Include documentation from the embassy/airline if possible.

Allison: should managers pre-approve or just submit after?

Asha (People Ops): Ideally pre-approve when possible (manager + People Ops). For true emergencies, submit after and mark as EMERGENCY. Finance will fast-track those flagged in the workflow.

Grant (Finance): Confirmed — we’ll prioritize expensing and processing for anything marked `EMERGENCY`. Expect faster turnaround for payments/advances where needed.

HR-Bot: Document updated by Asha (People Ops) — https://redwood.inc/policies/emergency-leave-v2 (version 2.0, effective today).

Asha (People Ops): Also a quick reminder about conduct while traveling: company Code of Conduct applies on all business/personal travel when representing Redwood. If you’re uncertain about what qualifies, email travel@redwood.com or drop into the Q&A session next Wednesday 11:00 AM PT (30 min).

Jin: Thanks — I’ll share with the on-call folks. :pray:

Allison: Sharing with my team now.

Mike (Legal): If anyone has questions about the paperwork for large reimbursements, DM me.

Asha (People Ops): Thanks everyone. If you need help filing, ping me or use the travel@redwood.com inbox. We’ll keep an internal log for audit and to help surface recurring gaps. :memo:
